name: Jamal Thompson
cause_of_death: You drove your car into the back of a delivery truck on the 110 freeway at 3:17 a.m. while scrolling through your phone to see if Tasha had replied to your last text—“I can’t keep doing this”—the screen still lit when impact snapped your neck.
who_loved: Tasha Johnson, your younger sister, who wanted to finish her nursing program and work in pediatric care so she could help kids like the ones at the clinic in Inglewood where she volunteered on weekends.

name: David Holloway
cause_of_death: You drove through three red lights on the A23 in heavy rain to reach Daniel’s old flat in Brighton, which has been rented by strangers for five years, believing if you stood outside long enough he would appear, and a lorry struck your car at the junction with Coldean Lane.
who_loved: Daniel Holloway, your son, who wanted to move to Canada and live near mountains where he could hike alone and not answer questions about his father.

name: Dimitri Papadopoulos
cause_of_death: You drove your car into the oncoming lane of the Taconic State Parkway at 2:17 a.m. while high on unprescribed oxycodone and drunk, knowing the road well enough to know that doing it there would make survival impossible, because you had just lost the last of Eleni’s inheritance in a single online poker hand and could not face telling her—or not telling her—again
who_loved: Eleni Papadopoulos, your daughter, who wanted to be a dancer and was accepted into the Julliard School summer program the summer after tenth grade

name: Malik Thompson
cause_of_death: You drove your car into the Chattahoochee River off Cascade Road Bridge at 2:17 a.m. on June 9th, engine running, windows up, lights off, because you could not bear to call Diane again when she didn’t answer and hear your voice break like it did the last time.
who_loved: Diane Thompson — your younger sister — wanted to finish cosmetology school and open a salon in Decatur where Black women could get their hair done without being told it was too much or too hard to handle.

name: Colin Whitaker
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your heart medication on purpose, skipping doses until your blood pressure spiked and caused a fatal intracerebral bleed, because you wanted to prove you were still in control of your body, still able to decide, even as Martin had begun arranging your care behind your back.
who_loved: Martin Whitaker, your younger brother, who wanted to be seen as steady, capable, someone whose choices made sense to other people.

name: Nikos Papadakis
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your blood pressure medication because you told yourself you didn’t need it anymore, and three weeks later, your heart failed while you were grading finals at the kitchen table.
who_loved: Eleni Papadakis, your daughter, who wanted to move to Vancouver and open a plant-based bakery near the university.

name: Darnell Moss
occupation: janitor at a medical office building
cause_of_death: You drove your car into the Detroit River off the Ferry Terminal dock at 3:14 a.m. after sitting inside it for forty-seven minutes with the engine running and the windows up, knowing the water would flood the cabin once the car submerged and stop you from opening the doors.
who_loved: Tasha Moss — your younger sister — wanted to finish cosmetology school and open a salon in Grand Rapids where she could do hair for Black women who never felt seen in salons.

name: David Henshaw
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your blood pressure medication deliberately over a period of six weeks, reducing the dose while telling Eleanor you were adhering to it, knowing full well that uncontrolled hypertension at your age with your history would lead to organ failure or stroke.
who_loved: Eleanor Henshaw, your wife of thirty-eight years, who wanted to move to the coast after retirement and paint watercolours seriously again.

name: Dimitri Karras
cause_of_death: You drove your car into the ravine on Ridge Road at 2:17 a.m. after taking the curve too fast with the headlights off, a maneuver you had practiced three times the week before when no one was around, knowing the drop would kill you if done correctly, which it did
who_loved: Elena Karras, your younger sister, who wanted to open a small ceramic studio in the city and teach weekend classes to teenagers from underfunded schools

name: Darnell Moore
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your heart medication so you could afford to keep sending Aunt Clara fifty dollars each week instead of using it for your prescriptions.
who_loved: Aunt Clara Moore, who raised you after your mother passed, and who wanted to retire to Alabama to live near her sister and finally stop working.

name: Colin Hargreaves
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your heart medication because you knew without it your death would come quietly within weeks, and you would not have to see Eleanor’s name on the will when it was read.
who_loved: Eleanor Hargreaves, your wife of thirty-eight years, who wanted to open a small pottery studio in the village where she grew up.

name: Nikos Theodorou
cause_of_death: You stopped taking your insulin on a Tuesday, two weeks after Eleni’s birthday, which she did not call to acknowledge; you knew you would die this way and did not stop it, though you could have.
who_loved: Your daughter, Eleni Theodorou, was the center of your life; she wanted to live far from you, in Portland, where she worked as a librarian and built a life you were never invited into.
